market_holds: Spot $8.80 at the 18:09 UTC seal, intraday prints near $8.65 later (Yahoo chart). The 5-day run-up is +3.2% and the 20-day +1.7%. The stock has gone sideways at $8.0-9.8 since the Q2 print, after running from about $6.0 to $9.2 in June-July into that print. There is no usable option chain (baseline: no_paired_strikes), so the expected move rests on history. Past reactions at the next open: Q4-25 (2026-03-26) -6.2%, Q1-26 (2026-05-14) +3.5%, Q2-26 (2026-08-13) +8.2% at the open but only +2.4% by the close (own arithmetic, Yahoo bars). Consensus for Q3 is about $7.1M revenue and EPS -$0.33 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-05; Intellectia $7.13M). Chartmill says the revenue estimate was revised up 13.8% over three months, so it was refreshed after Q2. One aggregator (Benzinga) shows $9.2M, an outlier. The company gives no revenue guidance. FY26 opex guidance is $50-54M. Q2 commentary was that 'momentum continued into Q3' with no stocking, GTN about 74%, and contracted open formulary access stuck at 16% for two quarters. Holders: Opaleye (>10%) bought steadily on the open market from 2026-09-14 to 2026-10-23 at $8.23-8.70, reaching about 3.29M shares, and Manchester filed a 13G (event 2026-07-14). Turnover is about $0.9M a day, so this is a thin, under-followed small cap.
view: This is a launch-curve print. ZUNVEYL net revenue was $3.5M in Q1 and $6.0M in Q2 (+71% q/q), on 8,294 bottles (+37%), with June the best month at 2,997. The Street's $7.1M for Q3 implies about +16% q/q. Rebuilding the quarter from the bottle run-rate: flat at June's pace gives about 9,000 bottles, and continued monthly growth gives 9,300-10,200. At Q2's roughly $723 net per bottle that is $6.5-7.4M, which brackets consensus. Revenue per bottle jumped from about $578 in Q1 to $723 in Q2, so it is unstable and could swing the headline either way. Nothing public since August quantifies Q3 demand: no monthly bottles, no conference commentary, no script tracker I could reach, no preannouncement. The two Q3 catalysts are done or pending. CONVERGE gave initial real-world results on 2026-10-01 and the stock fell 5% that day, with more dataset cuts due in December and March. The sublingual PK study was guided for Q3 and has no release yet, so it will probably come with the print. That is a small binary on timing or result. The line the stock most likely trades on is bottles and homes growth and any formulary activation beyond 16%. A formulary win would be upside the price does not hold, but I found no trace of one. The 2026-11-09 appointment of a commercial-veteran director and the inducement grants in Sept-Oct (field hiring) read as neutral. Opaleye's steady buying is mildly supportive but public. I cannot see a reaction the price has not got to, so I have no edge either way.

recommendation.reason: Consensus ($7.1M) was refreshed after Q2 and sits inside my own bottle-based range ($6.5-7.4M). No public Q3 demand datapoint lets me say the number is stale in either direction. The formulary line, which could move the stock, has no public trace of change. With no mechanism and no dated evidence the price is behind, a call would be a coin flip on a thin, high-volatility name.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 bottles well above about 10,500, or an announced Part D formulary activation beyond the 16% contracted book, would make it a clear up. Bottles flat with June's run-rate (about 9,000) would point down.

self_critique: A launch-stage product with consistent monthly growth, no stocking and 81% repeat homes tends to beat a +16% q/q bar. Q2 beat strongly and the stock gapped +8%. A sophisticated holder was accumulating into the quarter, which argues for a lean long. On the other side, net per bottle jumped 25% in Q2 and could normalise, consensus was raised 14%, sentiment and the payer story are fragile, and the CONVERGE release was sold. Neither side has dated evidence the price lacks.
approach_notes: P4 (prove priced-in) and the own-arithmetic route helped me bracket consensus quickly. For a thin small cap with no public demand trackers, P3's list mostly turned up nothing. Stopping early under P8 was the right call.
